title: Why we shun altars, statues and temples
source_text: Εἰσὶν οὖν τινες τῶν δικαίων ἄνθραξ λίθος καὶ ἄλλοι σάπφειρος καὶ ἄλλοι ἴασπις καὶ ἄλλοι κρύσταλλος· καὶ οὕτω πᾶν γένος ἐκλεκτῶν καὶ τιμίων λίθων εἰσὶν οἱ δίκαιοι. τὸν δὲ περὶ λίθων νοῦν καὶ τῆς φύσεως αὐτῶν λόγον. καὶ εἰς ποδαπὰς ψυχὰς ἀναφέρεσθαι δύναται ἐκ τοῦ τιμίου λίθου τὸ ὄνομα, οὐ κατὰ τὸν παρόντα καιρόν ἐστι διηγήσασθαι· μόνον δ᾿ ἐχρῆν ὑπομνησθῆναι ἐπ᾿ ὀλίγον τοῦ βουλήματος τῶν καθ᾿ ἡμᾶς ναῶν καὶ ἑνὸς τοῦ ἐκ λίθων τιμίων νεὼ τοῦ θεοῦ. ὥσπερ γὰρ, εἰ ἐπὶ τοῖς νομιζομένοις ναοῖς ἕκαστοι κατὰ τὰς σφῶν πόλεις ἐσεμνύνοντο πρὸς τοὺς ἑτέρους, ἔλεγον ἂν οἱ ἐπὶ τοῖς τιμιωτέροις ναοῖς μέγα φρονοῦντες τὰ ἐξαίρετα τῶν ἰδίων εἰς ἔλεγχον τῶν ὑποδεεστέρων· οὕτως πρὸς τοὺς ἐγκαλοῦντας ἡμῖν, ἐπεὶ μὴ νομίζομεν δεῖν σέβειν τὸ θεῖον παρ᾿ ἀναισθήτοις ναοῖς, ἀντιπαραλαμβάνομεν τοὺς καθ᾿ ἡμᾶς ναοὺς καὶ δείκνυμεν τοῖς γε μὴ ἀναισθήτοις μηδὲ παραπλησίοις τοῖς ἀναισθήτοις θεοῖς αὐτῶν ὅτι οὐδεμία σύγκρισίς ἐστιν οὔτε τῶν παρ᾿ ἡμῖν ἀγαλμάτων πρὸς τὰ ἀγάλματα τῶν ἐθνῶν οὔτε τῶν παρ᾿ ἡμῖν βωμῶν καὶ τῶν παρ᾿ αὐτοῖς, ἵν᾿ οὕτως ὀνομάσω, θυμιαμάτων πρὸς τοὺς ἐκείνων βωμοὺς καὶ τὰς παρ᾿ αὐτοῖς κνίσσας καὶ αἵματα ἀλλ᾿ οὐδὲ τῶν ἀποδεδομένων ναῶν πρὸς τοὺς ναοὺς τῶν ἀναισθήτων, ὑπὸ αναισθήτων ἀνθρώπων θαυμαζομένων καὶ μηδὲ φαντασιωθέντων τὴν θείαν αἴσθησιν, ᾗ αἰσθάνεταί τις θεοῦ καὶ τῶν τούτου ἀγαλμάτων καὶ ναῶν καὶ βωμῶν, πρεπόντων θεῷ. οὐκ εἰς τὸ πιστὸν οὖν ἀφανοῦς καὶ ἀποῤῥήτου κοινωνίας καὶ τὸ τοιοῦτο σύνθημα φεύγομεν βωμοὺς καὶ ἀγάλματα καὶ νεὼς ἱδρύεσθαι, ἀλλ᾿ ὅτι εὑρόντες διὰ τὴν Ἰησοῦ διδασκαλίαν τὸν τρόπον τῆς εἰς τὸ θεῖον εὐσεβείας φεύγομεν τὰ φαντασίᾳ εὐσεβείας ἀσεβεῖς ποιοῦντα τοὺς ἐσφαλμένους ἀπὸ τῆς διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εὐσεβείας· ὅς ἐστι μόνος „ὁδὸς“ εὐσεβείας, ἀληθῶς λέγων τό· „ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ὁδὸς καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια καὶ ἡ ζωή.“
pass_a_gloss: There are, then, some of the righteous (δίκαιοι) carbuncle stone (ἄνθραξ λίθος) and others sapphire and others jasper and others crystal; and thus the righteous are every kind (γένος) of chosen (ἐκλεκτοί) and precious (τίμιοι) stones. But the sense (νοῦς) about stones and the account (λόγος) of their nature (φύσις), and to what sort of (ποδαπός) souls the name (ὄνομα) from the precious stone can be referred (ἀναφέρω), it is not according to the present occasion (καιρός) to narrate (διηγέομαι); it was needed only to be reminded (ὑπομιμνήσκω) briefly of the intent (βούλημα) of the temples among us and of the one temple (νεώς) of God from precious stones. For just as, if on the reputed (νομιζόμενοι) temples each people according to their own cities prided themselves (σεμνύνομαι) against the others, those thinking big (μέγα φρονέω) on the more precious temples would say the special excellences (ἐξαίρετα) of their own toward refuting/exposing (ἔλεγχος) the inferior (ὑποδεέστεροι); thus toward those accusing (ἐγκαλέω) us, since we do not think one must worship (σέβω) the divine (τὸ θεῖον) at senseless (ἀναίσθητοι) temples, we take up in opposition (ἀντιπαραλαμβάνω) the temples among us and show (δείκνυμι) to those at least not senseless nor resembling (παραπλήσιοι) their senseless gods that there is no comparison (σύγκρισις) either of the statues among us to the statues of the nations (ἔθνη), or of the altars among us and the, so to name them, incense (θυμιάματα) from them, to their altars and the burnt-fat savours (κνῖσαι) and bloods (αἵματα) among them; but neither of the temples rendered (ἀποδίδωμι) [by us] to the temples of the senseless, admired (θαυμάζω) by senseless men and not even having imagined (φαντασιόομαι) the divine sense (θεία αἴσθησις), by which one perceives (αἰσθάνομαι) God and his statues and temples and altars fitting to God. Not for the pledge (τὸ πιστόν) then of an unseen and secret (ἀπόρρητος) fellowship (κοινωνία) and such a token (σύνθημα) do we flee setting up altars and statues and temples, but because, having found (εὑρίσκω) through the teaching (διδασκαλία) of Jesus the manner (τρόπος) of piety (εὐσέβεια) toward the divine, we flee the things that by an appearance (φαντασία) of piety make impious (ἀσεβεῖς) those who have slipped (σφάλλομαι) from the piety through Jesus Christ; who alone is the way (ὁδός) of piety, truly saying: I am the way and the truth and the life (ζωή).
pass_b_english: Some of the righteous, then, are carbuncle stone, others sapphire, others jasper, others crystal (Isaiah 54:11–12); and so the righteous are every kind of choice and precious stone. The meaning to be found in these stones, the account of their nature, and the kinds of souls to which the name of each precious stone can be applied, this is not the occasion to set out. It was necessary only to recall briefly the intent of our temples, and of the one temple of God made of precious stones.

For suppose that people in their several cities were taking pride, one against another, in what they count as temples. Those who were proud of their more costly temples would speak of the special excellences of their own in order to show up the inferior ones. In the same way, to those who accuse us because we do not think the divine should be worshipped in senseless temples, we set our own temples against theirs. And we show, at least to those who are not senseless and not like their senseless gods, that there is no comparison between our statues and the statues of the Gentiles; nor between our altars, with what I may call the incense rising from them, and their altars with the smoke of burnt fat and the blood; nor yet between the temples we have described and the temples of senseless gods, admired by senseless men who have not so much as formed a notion of the divine sense (Proverbs 2:5) by which one perceives God and his statues and temples and altars, those that are fitting for God.

It is not, then, to keep faith with a hidden and secret fellowship, nor as any token of that kind, that we shun setting up altars and statues and temples. Rather, because through the teaching of Jesus we have found the manner of piety toward the divine, we shun the things that, under a show of piety, make impious those who have strayed from the piety that comes through Jesus Christ. He alone is the “way” of piety, and he says truly: “I am the way, and the truth, and the life” (John 14:6).

choices.choice: The opening list of stones applies the Isaiah 54:11-12 (Septuagint) passage quoted at the end of 8.19, and is cited to it. ‘The divine sense’ (θείαν αἴσθησιν) is Origen’s regular phrase from Proverbs 2:5 as he reads it, αἴσθησιν θείαν εὑρήσεις (‘you will find a divine sense’), which he quotes and attributes to Solomon at Against Celsus 1.48 (also 7.34); the common Septuagint text reads ἐπίγνωσιν θεοῦ εὑρήσεις (‘you will find knowledge of God’). Cited inline on Origen’s own attribution, as in 1.48. ‘Not like their senseless gods’ may echo Psalm 115:8 (Septuagint 113:16), ‘those who make them become like them’; not cited inline as the wording is not close. In ‘the temples of senseless gods, admired by senseless men’, the participle θαυμαζομένων may agree with the temples or with the senseless gods; the English keeps the same ambiguity, and ‘gods’ is supplied for τῶν ἀναισθήτων from ‘their senseless gods’ just before. τῶν ἐθνῶν is rendered ‘the Gentiles’. κνῖσαι is rendered ‘the smoke of burnt fat’, without the added scorn of ‘reek’. τῶν ἀποδεδομένων ναῶν (‘the temples we have described’) means the temples set out in the preceding argument. The final clause repeats Celsus’s charge from 8.17 (‘keep faith with a hidden and secret fellowship’, ‘token’), rendered with the same words. τὸν τρόπον is rendered ‘the manner’, to keep it distinct from ὁδός (‘way’) at the close. ὑπὸ αναισθήτων lacks a breathing in the source; read as ἀναισθήτων.
Proverbs 2:5 note corrected: the common LXX reads 'knowledge of God'; citation kept on Origen's own attribution (1.48)
restored γάρ ('For suppose'); μέγα φρονοῦντες 'were proud of', not 'thought highly of'
κνῖσαι 'smoke of burnt fat', not loaded 'reek'; ἔθνη 'Gentiles'
comma fixed so 'his statues and temples and altars' are objects of 'perceives'
